weather.tip: Clear and cool right now, but an 80% chance of rain later today — carry an umbrella and build in extra travel time this evening if Ganesha immersion processions are on your route.

around.headline: Bengaluru Class 8 student threatened, forced to hand over Rs 6 lakh in cash and gold
around.summary: A school student in Bengaluru was threatened and coerced into handing over Rs 6 lakh in cash and gold, per NDTV. If you or a family member face a similar threat, don't comply quietly — report immediately to the police control room (100) or the cyber crime helpline (1930).

around.headline: Bengaluru government schools may shift to earlier start times to ease peak-hour traffic
around.summary: Authorities are considering moving government school start times earlier to spread out peak-hour congestion, per The Siasat Daily. If adopted, expect school-zone traffic to shift earlier in the morning.

around.headline: 750-metre Sadahalli Junction underpass planned to ease Bengaluru traffic
around.summary: A new underpass at Sadahalli Junction is being built to cut congestion in the area, per The Times of India. Expect construction-related detours nearby until it's completed.

around.headline: Bengaluru civic body plans data-driven waste management overhaul, 'nuisance detectors' on the cards
around.summary: The city corporation is planning a data-driven revamp of waste collection, including sensors to flag illegal dumping, per The Times of India. This could mean quicker action on garbage black-spot complaints in your ward.

around.headline: Bengaluru woman wins Rs 1.8 lakh after cosmetic treatment firm's promised results fall flat
around.summary: A consumer forum awarded a Bengaluru woman Rs 1.8 lakh in compensation after a cosmetic/beauty treatment firm failed to deliver its promised results, per The Times of India. Keep receipts and any written promises for paid treatments — that's what a consumer forum acts on.

around.headline: Wholesale inflation (WPI) rises to 9.92% in August on food, fuel and manufactured goods
around.summary: India's Wholesale Price Index inflation climbed to 9.92% in August, driven by food, fuel and manufactured-goods prices, per The Hindu. Sustained wholesale inflation typically feeds through to retail prices in the following months.

events.name: Gauri-Ganesh immersion processions across Bengaluru
events.note: Temples and lakes across the city continue to see huge crowds as Gauri-Ganesh immersion processions continue, with heavy traffic reported on immersion routes for a second straight day, per Udayavani and indiatoday.in.

events.name: Civic immersion tankers for Ganesha idols
events.note: 659 mobile tankers and 42 fixed tanks have been set up across Bengaluru as designated eco-friendly immersion points for Ganesha idols, per The New Indian Express — a greener alternative to immersing idols directly in lakes.

events.name: Community plogging and herb-planting drives
events.note: Residents across Bengaluru have been organising plogging (jogging plus litter-picking) and herb-planting drives in neighbourhood parks, per The Times of India — worth joining if one is active near you.

street_smart.title: Your teenage child comes home shaken, saying someone threatened them and demanded the family hand over cash and gold right away — the same kind of threat that forced a Bengaluru Class 8 student to hand over Rs 6 lakh in cash and gold, reported today. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: NDTV, Sept 14/15 — a Bengaluru Class 8 student was threatened and forced to hand over Rs 6 lakh in cash and gold; the headline doesn't detail exactly how the threat was made, so this scenario generalizes the underlying mechanism — an extortion threat coercing a family into handing over valuables — and hasn't been used as a street-smart scenario in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: Whoever made the threat wants an answer within the hour and has warned against involving the police, saying they're watching to see if you comply.

choices.text: Don't hand over anything yet. Call the police control room (100) or the cyber crime helpline (1930) immediately, and preserve every message, call log or note from the threat as evidence.
choices.feedback: Correct. A threat that says 'don't call the police' is trying to stop you from doing the one thing that actually protects you. Police can act faster and more safely than a family paying alone, and preserved evidence is what makes that action possible.

choices.text: Quietly gather the cash and gold and hand it over as demanded, so the threat ends immediately and no one gets hurt.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Paying doesn't end an extortion threat — it confirms you'll comply, which invites repeat demands. It also destroys the one chance to involve police before valuables leave your hands.

choices.text: Try to negotiate the amount down yourself and arrange the handover somewhere you feel is safe, without telling anyone else.
choices.feedback: Risky. Handling it alone still means one family facing an unknown threat with no backup, and a lower payment is still compliance — it doesn't remove the danger or stop further demands.

choices.text: Tell close relatives what happened and decide together as a family whether to pay, without contacting the police.
choices.feedback: Risky. More people knowing helps, but keeping the police out removes the one party equipped to trace the threat and stop it — this is exactly what the threat is counting on.

takeaways: Any threat that specifically warns you not to involve the police is telling you that police involvement is exactly what would stop it — call 100 or 1930 (cybercrime.gov.in) right away.
Preserve every message, call recording, number or note connected to the threat; it's what investigators need to act, and it's lost the moment you comply and move on.
When a minor is targeted or endangered, Childline (1098) is a dedicated helpline built for exactly that situation.

quiz.question: What was a Bengaluru Class 8 student reportedly threatened into handing over, per NDTV?
options: Rs 6 lakh in cash and gold
quiz.why: The report gave no further detail on how the threat was carried out — a reminder that a threat demanding you not involve police is itself a signal to do exactly that.

quiz.question: How many Bengaluru hospitals were supplied counterfeit cancer drugs by an arrested pharmacy owner, per this week's reports?
quiz.why: If a family member is on cancer treatment via a third-party pharmacy, it's worth asking the hospital to confirm the batch and manufacturer of the drug.

quiz.question: India's Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation rose to what level in August, per The Hindu?
quiz.why: WPI tracks prices at the wholesale/producer level; sustained rises here tend to show up in retail prices with a lag of a few months.

quiz.question: Which river is Bengaluru's principal source of drinking water, pumped over 100 km uphill to the city?
quiz.why: Bengaluru has no major river of its own, which is why it historically relied on a chain of lakes and now depends heavily on Cauvery water pumped a long distance, plus groundwater.

quiz.question: What is the term for the interest rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks?
quiz.why: When the RBI cuts the repo rate, banks' own borrowing gets cheaper, which usually (with a lag) brings down loan EMIs for consumers too.
